viralClaimVerdict.claim: Changing object key order makes property access roughly 10x slower
viralClaimVerdict.measured: 1.14x slower for inverted key order alone, with its own call site
viralClaimVerdict.alsoMeasured: 1.11x for two shapes sharing one call site
viralClaimVerdict.whatIsActuallyTrue: The real order-of-magnitude cliff is dictionary mode from `delete`: 8.9x after a single delete and 24.3x after add/delete churn. Megamorphic spread at 16 shapes costs 4.35x.

findings: V8 14.6 is far more tolerant of shape diversity than the viral posts assume. Two shapes at one call site cost only 1.11x; four cost 1.27x.
Spreading, Object.assign, destructuring, class constructors and JSON round-trips are all within noise of the baseline when measured in isolation.
The megamorphic cliff is real but sits much higher than claimed: at 16 shapes the penalty jumps to 4.35x.
`delete` is the real trap. One delete already costs 8.9x; a 16-property add/delete churn costs 24.3x.
Corrected narrative for content: stop repeating the key-order claim. Teach that the cliff comes from `delete` and from exceeding ~16 shapes per call site.
